text: Your successor kept the songs and sold the halls. The movement survived as a mailing list, and then as a brand of energy drink.
The unions became a benevolent society, then a call centre. The cities kept the murals, because murals are cheap.
Nobody could say any more what the movement had wanted. The archive burned in an uninsured warehouse, and the anniversary was still observed.
Your successor consulted widely and decided little. The working groups outlived the problems they were convened to study.
Generations of committees, each genuinely representative, each slightly too late. The buses ran, mostly.
Centuries on, the country is a footnote in somebody else's history, and honestly not a bad one.
Your successor inherited a clinic in every district and the habit of publishing the accounts. The habit turned out to matter more.
The halls became libraries, the libraries became schools, and the schools produced people who found the whole story faintly embarrassing.
The country is remembered for its water and its buses, which is the kind of monument that keeps working.
Your successor was a nephew. The ministries stayed in the family, and the family stopped being worth marrying into.
Six names and a bishop ran the counties. Tax was voluntary in practice, and the roads showed it.
The last engineer died without an apprentice. The garbage, at least, was very well advertised.
Your successor changed nothing and was praised for steadiness. The budget balanced because half of it was not looked at.
Generations of orderly stagnation. The flag was respected, the schools were adequate, and the clever ones left.
Centuries on, the country is stable, courteous and some way behind, and would not have it otherwise.
Your successor was picked by a committee that met in public, which was new. The donors complained, and stayed.
The schools produced engineers. The engineers produced ships. The ships were dull and safe and left on schedule.
The country is remembered for being solvent, orderly and dull, which its neighbours prefer to call luck.
